REQ-1: Update server to run Debian 12 Bookworm version and install Wireguard Kernel module wireguard.ko to support Wireguard configuration. Implement kernel-based verification for Wireguard operation not to rely on userspace implementation.
REQ-2: Configure the server to create a single WireGuard interface per VPN instance running on the server. The interface should be called wg0 and assigned IP address 10.64.0.1 24, with 10.64.0.0 24 subnet reserved exclusively for Wireguard tunnel addressing. The interface should be managed via wg-quick@wg0 using the systemd service manager.
REQ-3: Changes to peer configuration on the server should be performed without restarting the Wireguard interface, not to affect existing connections. Furthermore, Wireguard interface should be automatically restored to normal state after server reboot.
REQ-4: Enable wireguard interface to listen on UDP port 51820. Whitelist this port on the server firewall and upstream security controls to ensure successful connection to the server. Port changes are to be supported only via controlled maintenance.
REQ-5: The server private key is generated using Curve25519 and store it in server.key path. The file permissions should allow only the owner to read or modify the file, while other users should have no access to the key for security. The corresponding public key should be exposed for client provisioning and configuration files are readable not only from root user.
REQ-6: Server allows only a single peer connection for a single identified client device. Each peer should be uniquely identifiable using the client public key. No other information about the user should be available on the server.
REQ-7: Each connecting client has to be assigned a unique IPv4 address in the provided range: 10.64.0.2-10.64.0.254. For connection, each peer has to specify AllowedIPs = as client IP address in the 32 subnet.
REQ-8: IP forwarding has to be enabled on the server using net.ipv4.ip_forward=1. This should be configured on initial server setup and persist on every server reboot, unless the initialization script would be updated.
REQ-9: Set up NAT masquerading for tunnel traffic that is exiting via the primary interface.
REQ-10: Implement support for live perr add, update or remove operations using the wg set command. All peer configurations should be persistent and saved in the wg0.conf file. Peer configuration validation also has to be implemented to detect and reject malformed or otherwise invalid configurations.
REQ-11: The server needs to have separate containers, each having a running Wireguard configuration on them, to allow using a single physical server as multiple Wireguard VPN servers. All of them should use identical configuration structure and setup.
REQ-12: Initial version of wireguard servers should have these logs enabled on it for observability: interface state changes, peer add and remove events, handshake initiation events (without logging any user traffic for no logs policy upkeep) and health checks indicating wireguard interface status. All of these should be logged on the server, including a timestamp.
REQ-13: For security reasons the entire system should: use wireguard fixed cryptographic primitives only, ensure cryptographic configuration options are not exposed in any way, use existing guidelines for Wireguard certificates or TLS tunnels, only use cryptographic methods for authentication, instead of usernames, passwords or MFA setup.
REQ-14: Windows app requires the ability to generate key pairs using Curve 25519, by using a cryptographically secure RNG. We need to ivnestigate and implement a secure storing solution for the private keys, to ensure they are never compromised.
REQ-15: Implement private key storage using Windows Data Protection API. The keys should be encrypted on the device using a separate algorithm and accessible only for the user, that generated the keys.
REQ-16: Before sending the public key, we need to use Base64 encoding using the provided backend API call and bearer authorization method.
REQ-17: In DB, public key should be associated with corresponding customer ID and device ID (as each customer can have multiple devices used for connection). Key should also have association with server ID, to know to which server it was used to connect. Lastly, the assigned IP address should be stored, to ensure it is not assigned to a different user.
REQ-18: We require to have a call implemented, that would allow to revoke a provided peer. The call should remove the peer entry from the server and mark it as rewoked, which should leave to user not being able to establish a new connection to the server (due to his keys being revoked). Key creation and revocation timestamps should be tracked for observalibility.
REQ-19: Key rotation needs to be supported for user connections. With this functionality we need to prevent the reuse or revoked public keys and make sure that if a new key is used, the previous one if invalidated or revoked immediately.
REQ-20: We need to integrate the offocial wireguard kernel driver for Windows to support wireguard connection. A check should be implemented before tunnel creation, to verify that the driver is loaded. In case it is not loaded yet, an error should be returned for user.
REQ-21: wg.exe and wg-quick should not be invoked during runtime and instead Wireguard Windows service API should be used for tunnel management.
REQ-22: When establishing a tunnel app should configure the server endpoint as <server_ip>:51820, using the server IP address returned by the api or availableServers endpoint. During successful connection, app will get the IPv4 address assigned for the created tunnel, or an error message indicating that a tunnel already exists, blocking the connection attempt.
REQ-23: App has to support full tunnel routing using AllowedIPs functionality and split tunneling routing via the use of explicit CIDR ranges. Based on user selection app should use full tunnel or split tunneling approach.
REQ-24: To keep the connection running, client-side should implement a keep alive ping once every 25 seconds using the backend library. In case endpoint IP change is detected, app should reinitiate the handshake and inform the user of connection instability.
REQ-25: Windows app logs should include last handshake timestamp, RX byte counters, TX byte counters, an alert that tunnel is connected (only generate it if a handshake occured within 120) or disconnected (if handshake took more than 120 seconds, consider it timeout).
REQ-26: Implement handling for network connection changes (from Wi-fi to Ethernet). During this change, we should not lose the VPN connection and handle the IP address change on the local interface.
REQ-27: We need to support multiple tunnel profiles, while also preventing simultaneous activation of conflicting tunnels. Furthermore, handshake failure state or endpoint unreachable states should be surfaced and both logged in logs and shown in the app as error for user (with ability to reconnect).
REQ-28: If user decides to disconnect from the server, tunnel should be terminanted and all system resources released. The same procedure should be carried out if application is closed or device shutdown is initiated.
REQ-29: Wireguard driver installation should be done using a signed MSI installer during app install or update flow. For this, we need to request user to provide administrative privileges. During the installation, verify that Wireguard version is higher than 0.4.3 (lowest supported version) or return an error indicating that installation was not successful.
REQ-30: On app side, user should be able to switch between Wireguard and OpenVPN connection. In this case, the no longer needed tunnel should be terminated. Users protocol selection should be remembered between restarts and if user was connected before restart, a new connection should be initiated after the restart too. This connection should happen in the first 10 seconds after device is turned on or woken up from sleep.
REQ-31: Uninstalling the application should make sure to remove any changes done to the device firewall, any remaining tunnels or drivers should be removed. Virtual adapters created on the device should also be removed.
